violations.description: Refrigerated Storage. — --Refrigerator or cold storage was insufficient or ineffective at maintaining potentially hazardous food at a temperature of 41F or less. -Multiple food items were found at 43F or higher in the kitchen refrigerator. Upon further inspection it was found the refrigerator settings (a dial) was bumped to a warmer setting. All product was moved to the glass cooler and the setting was adjusted lower.

Date marking and disposition of ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food. — --Refrigerated, ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food (prepared more than 24 hours ago) was not properly date marked. -The glass cooler has multiple sauce bottles not labeled for contents and date marking. -Diced/sliced vegetables are not date marked and stored in the refrigerator.

General equipment and utensils - Maintenance and operation. — --Nonfood contact equipment/utensil was not maintained in a good repair or sound condition. -The refrigerator door interior material is broken and pulling away from the door. There is tape holding jars on a shelf.

Storage of cleaned equipment and utensils. — --Clean equipment/utensil was not stored in the proper location to protect from contamination. -Spoons are stored with the handle down in the utensil holder directly behind the toaster.

Date marking and disposition of ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food. — --Refrigerated, ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food (prepared more than 24 hours ago) was not properly date marked. Observed food containers in refrigerator did not have date marking.

General equipment and utensils - Materials and design. — --Material of nonfood contact surface was not constructed or designed to be smooth, nonabsorbent and cleanable. Observed food prep area had exposed wood that was not smooth and cleanable.
